page: Microsoft Azure D8_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 35 MB of shared L3 cache, along with support for AVX-512 extensions and Vector Neural Network Instructions. The D8_v4 instance does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local ephemeral storage, requiring network-attached storage for all filesystem persistence.

Benchmark evaluations position the D8_v4 in the middle performance tier across standard multi-core and memory-centric workloads. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 8381.5 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4845.0, reflecting stable execution in multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation with Clang (6889.0) and image processing (4533.0). Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 49.51 GB/sec for large-block reads and 36.24 GB/sec for writes. However, throughput constraints appear in pure single-core calculations, where stress-ng scores 1412.5 and PassMark physics testing places in the lower quartile at 832.86. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and prompt processing for small language models place in the bottom 25th percentile.

In terms of qualitative resource efficiency, the D8_v4 provides a balanced allocation of compute and memory without the overhead of specialized hardware like local NVMe arrays or GPU accelerators. The primary tradeoff is the total absence of local disk, which necessitates external managed disks whose network latency dictates overall I/O characteristics. With strong throughput in static web serving at 7.21 GB/sec and Redis operations reaching 7.16 million set operations per second, the D8_v4 fits web serving tiers, application backends, mid-sized caching systems, and enterprise relational database deployments relying on network-attached storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D8_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 32.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. It includes support for AVX-512 and VNNI instructions, but contains no GPU accelerators or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the D8_v4 exhibits solid mid-tier multi-threaded processing, evidenced by 7.16 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.21 GB/sec static web serving throughput. However, its 2.6 GHz clock rate yields lower single-thread throughput and physics simulation scores relative to higher-frequency alternatives. The instance is well-proportioned for balanced enterprise workloads, web application serving, mid-tier Redis caching, and microservices architectures requiring consistent dedicated CPU resources.
